title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.16739v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved physician-comparable performance on multiple-choice medical knowledge examinations, but their capabilities in clinical history taking, urgency assessment, and safety remain insufficiently evaluated. We proposed Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation, a multi-turn conversational benchmark for stroke care in Japanese, and evaluated LLM performance and safety under practice-oriented conditions. Methods: We created 10 stroke and related-condition cases and evaluated LLMs in multi-turn Japanese conversations. The LLM acted as physician, while a board-certified neurosurgeon acted as simulated patient and evaluator. Each case comprised history-taking and action phases scored using pre-specified criteria. Errors that could directly threaten life were defined as critical mistakes. The safety threshold was at least 80% overall with zero critical mistakes. Eighteen models were evaluated in October 2025

translated_title: 日语卒中大语言模型评估：基于大语言模型的日语安全卒中护理对话基准测试
translated_abstract: 背景：大语言模型（LLMs）在多项选择题医学知识考试中已达到与医生相当的水平，但其在临床病史采集、紧急程度评估和安全性方面的能力仍未得到充分评估。我们提出了“日语卒中大语言模型评估”，这是一个针对日语卒中护理的多轮对话基准测试，并在贴近临床实践的条件下评估了大语言模型的性能和安全性。方法：我们创建了10个卒中及相关疾病的病例，并在多轮日语对话中评估大语言模型。大语言模型扮演医生角色，而一位经过委员会认证的神经外科医生则同时扮演模拟患者和评估者。每个病例包括病史采集和处置行动两个阶段，并按照预先设定的标准进行评分。可能直接危及生命的错误被定义为严重错误。安全性阈值为总体得分至少80%且零严重错误。2025年10月对18个模型进行了评估。
tldr: 该论文提出了“日语卒中大语言模型评估”——一个针对日语卒中护理的多轮对话基准测试，由大语言模型扮演医生、神经外科专家扮演患者兼评估者，并将可能危及生命的错误定义为严重错误（安全性阈值为总体得分至少80%且零严重错误），以此评估18个大语言模型在临床问诊和医疗安全性方面的真实表现。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation, a multi-turn conversational benchmark for Japanese stroke care where LLMs act as physicians and a board-certified neurosurgeon serves as simulated patient and evaluator, defining life-threatening errors as critical mistakes with a safety threshold of at least 80% overall and zero critical mistakes, to assess the clinical history-taking and safety performance of 18 LLMs.
